title: NSAID-induced GI bleed: a predictable (pharmacologic) adverse drug reaction
topic: Adverse drug reactions - predictable vs unpredictable
vignette: A 35-year-old man comes to the emergency department due to acute onset coffee-ground emesis and lightheadedness. Two months ago, he developed lower back pain with stiffness and began taking naproxen and cyclobenzaprine. Medical history is notable for moderate persistent asthma, hepatitis C, and HIV. His last CD4 count was 550/mm3. The patient has a remote history of intravenous drug use but currently does not use any recreational drugs. He has an allergy to penicillin that causes a rash and pruritus. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy reveals gastric mucosal erythema and erosions. Which of the following best explains this patient's current symptoms?

clues.note: Coffee-ground emesis indicates upper GI bleeding - here from NSAID-induced gastric erosions.
Naproxen is an NSAID; NSAIDs inhibit cyclooxygenase, and GI mucosal injury/bleeding is a well-known, dose-related adverse effect.
Gastric erythema/erosions from NSAID use = a PREDICTABLE, pharmacologically expected adverse effect (loss of protective prostaglandins).

whatMatters: Upper GI bleeding from NSAID-induced gastric erosions is a PREDICTABLE (pharmacologic) ADVERSE DRUG REACTION - it results directly from the drug's KNOWN mechanism (cyclooxygenase inhibition reducing protective gastric prostaglandins). Answer D. Most adverse drug reactions are of this predictable type.
strategy: Classify the reaction. PREDICTABLE reactions follow from the drug's known pharmacology (dose-related, common) - e.g., NSAID -> reduced gastric prostaglandins -> gastritis/bleeding. UNPREDICTABLE reactions are patient-specific (immunologic or genetic). NSAID GI bleed = predictable. Reject exaggerated drug sensitivity/intolerance (unpredictable, occurs at low dose), idiosyncratic (genetic, e.g., G6PD), immunologic (drug allergy - like his penicillin rash), and pseudoallergic (direct mast-cell activation).

eliminations.label: Exaggerated drug sensitivity - unpredictable, low-dose (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an exaggerated (drug-intolerance) response - a known pharmacologic effect occurring at a LOWER dose than expected (patient-specific metabolism/susceptibility). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: NSAID gastric injury at a standard dose is the expected, PREDICTABLE effect, not an exaggerated low-dose response. ✅ Correct if: an expected effect appearing at an unusually low dose (e.g., TPMT-related azathioprine intolerance).

eliminations.label: Idiosyncratic reaction - patient-specific, not typical pharmacology
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an UNPREDICTABLE reaction from patient-specific factors that does NOT involve the drug's usual action (e.g., G6PD-deficiency hemolysis with sulfa). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: NSAID GI injury IS the drug's typical pharmacologic action, so it's predictable, not idiosyncratic. ✅ Correct if: an unusual, mechanism-independent reaction (G6PD hemolysis).

eliminations.label: Immunologic reaction - drug allergy (his penicillin rash)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an antibody- or T-cell-mediated hypersensitivity (drug allergy) - e.g., his penicillin rash/pruritus (IgE type I). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: gastric erosion/bleeding is a direct pharmacologic effect, not immune-mediated. ✅ Correct if: an allergic hypersensitivity reaction (rash, anaphylaxis).

eliminations.label: Pseudoallergic reaction - direct mast-cell activation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a reaction mimicking allergy via NONimmunologic mast-cell activation (e.g., vancomycin, opioids, radiocontrast). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: NSAID GI bleeding is not a mast-cell/allergy-mimic reaction. ✅ Correct if: an anaphylactoid reaction without IgE (vancomycin 'red man').

reasoning: Coffee-ground emesis + gastric erosions after starting naproxen = NSAID-induced upper GI bleeding
NSAIDs inhibit cyclooxygenase, reducing gastric prostaglandins that protect the mucosa
This adverse effect follows directly from the drug's known pharmacology (dose-related, common)
-> a predictable (pharmacologic) drug reaction; answer D
mechanism: Adverse drug reactions are broadly PREDICTABLE or UNPREDICTABLE. PREDICTABLE reactions arise from the drug's KNOWN pharmacologic properties, are usually DOSE-related and common, and often appear after extended exposure. NSAIDs (naproxen) inhibit CYCLOOXYGENASE (COX), which normally produces prostaglandins that maintain gastric mucosal protection (mucus/bicarbonate secretion, mucosal blood flow) in addition to their roles in platelet function and renal perfusion. Blocking COX therefore reduces protective prostaglandins, causing gastritis, erosions, ulceration, and GI BLEEDING (coffee-ground emesis) - a classic, EXPECTED (predictable) adverse effect that can appear within the first week of therapy. UNPREDICTABLE reactions are less common and are driven by patient-specific IMMUNOLOGIC or GENETIC factors: immunologic/allergic (e.g., his penicillin rash - IgE type I), idiosyncratic (e.g., G6PD-deficiency hemolysis with sulfa), exaggerated sensitivity/intolerance (a known effect at an unusually low dose, e.g., TPMT-related azathioprine intolerance), and pseudoallergic (nonimmune mast-cell activation, e.g., vancomycin/opioids/contrast). This patient's NSAID-induced GI bleed is the predictable, pharmacologically expected type.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Pharm > adverse drug reactions: PREDICTABLE (pharmacologic, dose-related - NSAID GI bleed via ↓gastric prostaglandins) vs UNPREDICTABLE (immunologic/allergic, idiosyncratic, pseudoallergic, exaggerated sensitivity).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: NSAID gastric injury follows from the drug's known mechanism -> predictable reaction.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on predictable vs unpredictable ADR, idiosyncratic, pseudoallergic, or cyclooxygenase/prostaglandins? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Exaggerated sensitivity/idiosyncratic/immunologic/pseudoallergic are UNPREDICTABLE (patient-specific); NSAID GI bleed is predictable.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: NSAID GI bleed = predictable pharmacologic ADR (↓protective gastric prostaglandins); unpredictable = immune/genetic.
